decisive_items: developed fever and erythema on trunk and extremities 3 days after receiving first dose of Moderna vaccine
Total occlusion of atrioventricular branch of right coronary artery
response.rationale: Vaccine-triggered fever/rash, marked systemic inflammation, and multi-organ arterial involvement (coronary occlusion/ectasia, renal/hepatic arterial lesions) in a young adult best fit multisystem inflammatory syndrome. Kawasaki disease is a mimic but adult age and incomplete mucocutaneous criteria make it secondary; ACS is a complication, not the underlying diagnosis.

rejected.why: Thrombocytopenia and thrombosis after vaccine, but D-dimer is only mildly elevated and Moderna mRNA plus coronary ectasia/multi-organ arteritis favor MIS rather than VITT.
Kawasaki disease mimic, but adult age and lack of classic mucocutaneous criteria make it less likely than MIS.
Arterial thrombosis and thrombocytopenia possible, but no antiphospholipid antibodies or typical APS features.
Thrombocytopenia and renal involvement, but no schistocytes/MAHA and coronary ectasia/arterial wall destruction are not TTP.
Too broad; vaccine-induced immune-mediated disease is a category, not the specific syndrome.
Too broad; autoimmune disorder does not capture the specific post-vaccine multisystem inflammatory phenotype.
Vasculitis is a component, but MIS is the more specific syndrome accounting for vaccine context and systemic inflammation.
Thrombophilia explains thrombosis but not fever, rash, coronary ectasia, or multi-organ inflammation.
ACS is the cardiac manifestation, not the underlying multisystem inflammatory diagnosis.
Thrombotic microangiopathy lacks schistocytes/MAHA and does not explain coronary ectasia/arterial destruction.
No specific support; immune-mediated thrombosis is too broad and less explanatory than MIS.
